blocks.tex:
Everything in the discrete layer so far is indexed by \emph{vertices}: the
turning angle $\theta_i$ of \cref{def:turning_angle} lives at vertex $i$ and
reads the two edges $\ell_{i-1}, \ell_i$ adjacent to it, and the moderate-arc
domain of \cref{def:moderate_arc} is likewise a per-vertex conjunction. This
chapter installs the complementary, \emph{edge}-indexed bookkeeping: each edge
$e$ carries a single scalar
\[
  \beta_e \;=\; \arcsin\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\kappa_e\,\ell_e}{2}\Bigr)
             \;+\; \arcsin\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\kappa_{e+1}\,\ell_e}{2}\Bigr),
\]
the \emph{gap} of that edge --- the total turn the development performs while
traversing $e$, split evenly between its two endpoints by the tangent-chord law.

The point of the change of variables is threefold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The turning sum becomes a plain sum of the new coordinates.}
  Regrouping the $2n$ arcsines of $T(\kappa,\ell)$ by the edge they mention
  instead of by the vertex that owns them gives $\sum_e \beta_e = T$
  (\cref{lem:gap_sum}). This is a re-indexing, nothing more, but it is what
  makes the constraint $T = 2\pi$ an \emph{affine} condition on the new
  coordinates rather than a transcendental one.
\item \textbf{The moderate-arc domain becomes a product of intervals.} The four
  wall inequalities that mention $\ell_e$ (two from each endpoint) collapse to
  the single two-sided bound $0 < \ell_e < 2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$
  (\cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}), and on that interval $\beta_e$ is a strictly
  increasing continuous bijection onto $(0, U_e)$ with the explicit wall
  \[
    U_e \;=\; \frac{\pi}{2}
       \;+\; \arcsin\frac{\min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
                         {\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
  \]
  (\cref{lem:gap_strict_mono,lem:gap_wall_value_cap}). So the whole strict
  domain, which in $\ell$-coordinates is a conjunction over vertices with
  overlapping constraints, is in $\beta$-coordinates literally the open box
  $\prod_e (0, U_e)$.
\item \textbf{It is the coordinate system of the external four-gap pipeline.}
  Writing $r_i = 1/\kappa_i$ for the osculating radii, the cap is
  $2\min(r_e,r_{e+1})$ and the wall is
  $\pi/2 + \arcsin\bigl(\min(r_e,r_{e+1})/\max(r_e,r_{e+1})\bigr)$
  (\cref{lem:gap_radius_cap,lem:gap_radius_wall}); the ratio appearing there is exactly the
  quantity called $a_i = L_i/H_i$ in that pipeline's notes. Note the inversion:
  a local \emph{minimum} of radius is a local \emph{maximum} of curvature, so a
  ``low'' $L$ in the radius word is a curvature peak.
\end{enumerate}

With the dictionary in place, the concluding statement of the pipeline's
realization arguments --- a gap vector $\beta$ with
$0 < \beta_k < U_k$ for all $k$, $\sum_k \beta_k = 2\pi$ and vanishing closure
--- is repackaged into $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$ by
\cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_vector}, with simplicity supplied for free by the
in-tree \cref{thm:convex_simple} (positive curvature $\Rightarrow$ convex
$\Rightarrow$ simple). The last section isolates, as a purely
order-theoretic lemma with no geometry in it, the global step of that
pipeline's zigzag argument (\cref{lem:high_neighbour_global}).

\medskip

\emph{Scope.} This chapter is a change of coordinates and a repackaging: it
proves no new realization. In particular it does not import, assume, or
depend on any of the pipeline's local four-gap certificates, all of which are
still under external audit; \cref{lem:high_neighbour_global} takes the
consequence it needs as an explicit hypothesis and is therefore vacuous until
someone supplies that hypothesis. Nothing here bears on
Tabachnikov's Problem~2.

blocks.title: The gap of an edge

blocks.tex:
Throughout, $n \ge 1$, $\kappa, \ell \colon \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}$, and
$e$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}/n$. Edge $e$ is the segment from vertex $e$ to
vertex $e+1$; it has length $\ell_e$ and its two endpoints carry curvatures
$\kappa_e$ and $\kappa_{e+1}$.

blocks.label: def:gap_angle
blocks.title: gap angle of an edge
blocks.body:
For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ put
  \[
    \gamma_e(t) \;=\;
      \arcsin\!\Bigl(\frac{\kappa_e\, t}{2}\Bigr)
      \;+\;
      \arcsin\!\Bigl(\frac{\kappa_{e+1}\, t}{2}\Bigr).
  \]
  This is the \emph{gap function} of edge $e$: the total turn contributed by an
  edge of length $t$ sitting between the two curvatures $\kappa_e,
  \kappa_{e+1}$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapAngleAt (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arcsin (κ e * (t / 2)) + Real.arcsin (κ (e + 1) * (t / 2))

blocks.label: def:gap_of_config
blocks.title: gap of a configuration
blocks.body:
The \emph{gap} of edge $e$ in the configuration $(\kappa,\ell)$ is
  $\beta_e = \gamma_e(\ell_e)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngle
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapAngle (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  gapAngleAt κ e (ℓ e)

blocks.label: def:edge_cap
blocks.title: edge cap
blocks.body:
For a curvature profile $\kappa$ set
  \[
    C_e \;=\; \frac{2}{\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})} .
  \]
  This is the \emph{edge cap}: the supremum of the lengths edge $e$ may take
  inside the strict moderate-arc domain (\cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap
lean.code:
noncomputable def edgeCap (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  2 / max (κ e) (κ (e + 1))

blocks.label: def:edge_wall
blocks.title: edge wall
blocks.body:
For a curvature profile $\kappa$ set
  \[
    U_e \;=\; \frac{\pi}{2}
      \;+\; \arcsin\frac{\min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})}
                        {\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})} .
  \]
  This is the \emph{edge wall}: the supremum of the gaps edge $e$ may take
  (\cref{lem:gap_wall_value_cap}).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeWall
lean.code:
noncomputable def edgeWall (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  Real.pi / 2 + Real.arcsin (min (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) / max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)))

blocks.label: lem:gap_sum
blocks.title: the turning sum is the sum of the gaps
blocks.body:
For $n \ge 1$ and any $\kappa, \ell$,
  \[
    \sum_{e \in \mathbb{Z}/n} \beta_e \;=\; T(\kappa,\ell).
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    By \cref{def:turning_angle},
    $T = \sum_i \bigl[\arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2)
       + \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_i/2)\bigr]$,
    which splits as $A + B$ with
    $A = \sum_i \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2)$ and
    $B = \sum_i \arcsin(\kappa_i \ell_i/2)$. Reindex $A$ by the bijection
    $i = e+1$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n$: it becomes
    $\sum_e \arcsin(\kappa_{e+1} \ell_e/2)$. Adding term by term,
    $A + B = \sum_e \bigl[\arcsin(\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e/2)
        + \arcsin(\kappa_e \ell_e/2)\bigr] = \sum_e \beta_e$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.sum_gapAngle
lean.code:
lemma sum_gapAngle [NeZero n] (κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    ∑ e : ZMod n, gapAngle κ ℓ e = turningSum κ ℓ := by
  unfold turningSum turningAngle gapAngle gapAngleAt
  simp only [tK_zero]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_comm]
  congr 1
  exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addRight (1 : ZMod n)) _ _
    (fun x => by simp [add_sub_cancel_right])

/-! ## The strict domain in edge coordinates -/

blocks.title: The strict domain in edge coordinates

blocks.label: lem:moderate_arc_edge
blocks.title: the moderate-arc domain is a box in $\ell$
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$. Then
  \[
    \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \forall e,\; 0 < \ell_e < C_e .
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    By \cref{lem:moderate_arc_zero}, $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$
    unfolds to: for every vertex $i$, $\ell_i > 0$,
    $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i-1}/2 < 1$ and $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_i/2 < 1$. Since
    $\kappa > 0$ we may drop the absolute values.

    ($\Rightarrow$) Fix $e$. Then $\ell_e > 0$; the right wall at vertex $e$
    gives $\kappa_e \ell_e/2 < 1$, and the left wall at vertex $e+1$ gives
    $\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e / 2 < 1$. Hence
    $\max(\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1})\,\ell_e/2 < 1$, i.e.\ $\ell_e < C_e$
    (the max is positive, so the division is legitimate).

    ($\Leftarrow$) Fix a vertex $i$. Positivity of $\ell_i$ is immediate. The
    hypothesis at $e = i$ gives $\ell_i < C_i \le 2/\kappa_i$, so
    $\kappa_i \ell_i/2 < 1$; the hypothesis at $e = i-1$ gives
    $\ell_{i-1} < C_{i-1} \le 2/\kappa_{i}$ (because $\kappa_i$ is one of the
    two curvatures entering $C_{i-1}$, namely the one at $(i-1)+1 = i$), so
    $\kappa_i \ell_{i-1}/2 < 1$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.moderateArc_zero_iff_edge
lean.code:
lemma moderateArc_zero_iff_edge {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ ↔ ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < ℓ e ∧ ℓ e < edgeCap κ e := by
  rw [moderateArc_zero_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h e
    have hmax : 0 < max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) := lt_max_iff.2 (Or.inl (hκ e))
    obtain ⟨hpos, -, hr⟩ := h e
    obtain ⟨-, hl', -⟩ := h (e + 1)
    rw [abs_of_pos (hκ e)] at hr
    rw [abs_of_pos (hκ (e + 1)), add_sub_cancel_right] at hl'
    exact ⟨hpos, lt_edgeCap_of_walls hmax hr hl'⟩
  · intro h i
    have hpos : 0 < ℓ i := (h i).1
    have hpos' : 0 < ℓ (i - 1) := (h (i - 1)).1
    refine ⟨hpos, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [abs_of_pos (hκ i)]
      exact mul_half_lt_one_of_lt_edgeCap (hκ i)
        (by rw [sub_add_cancel]; exact le_max_right _ _) hpos'.le (h (i - 1)).2
    · rw [abs_of_pos (hκ i)]
      exact mul_half_lt_one_of_lt_edgeCap (hκ i) (le_max_left _ _) hpos.le
        (h i).2

/-! ## The gap function is a bijection onto `(0, U_e)` -/

blocks.label: lem:edge_cap_pos
blocks.title: cap positivity
blocks.body:
If $\kappa_e > 0$ and $\kappa_{e+1} > 0$ then $C_e > 0$, and moreover
  $\kappa_e\,C_e/2 \le 1$ and $\kappa_{e+1}\,C_e/2 \le 1$ with equality in at
  least one of the two.
  \begin{proof}
    
    $\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1}) > 0$, so $C_e = 2/\max > 0$. For each of the
    two curvatures $\kappa \in \{\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1}\}$ we have
    $\kappa \le \max$, hence $\kappa\, C_e/2 = \kappa/\max \le 1$, with
    equality for whichever attains the maximum.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap_pos
lean.code:
lemma edgeCap_pos {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    0 < edgeCap κ e ∧ κ e * (edgeCap κ e / 2) ≤ 1 ∧
      κ (e + 1) * (edgeCap κ e / 2) ≤ 1 ∧
      (κ e * (edgeCap κ e / 2) = 1 ∨ κ (e + 1) * (edgeCap κ e / 2) = 1) := by
  have hmax : 0 < max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) := lt_max_iff.2 (Or.inl h)
  have hhalf : edgeCap κ e / 2 = (max (κ e) (κ (e + 1)))⁻¹ := by
    rw [edgeCap]
    field_simp
  refine ⟨div_pos two_pos hmax, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hhalf, ← div_eq_mul_inv, div_le_one hmax]
    exact le_max_left _ _
  · rw [hhalf, ← div_eq_mul_inv, div_le_one hmax]
    exact le_max_right _ _
  · rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
    · exact Or.inr (by rw [hhalf, max_eq_right hle, mul_inv_cancel₀ h'.ne'])
    · exact Or.inl (by rw [hhalf, max_eq_left hle, mul_inv_cancel₀ h.ne'])

blocks.label: lem:gap_strict_mono
blocks.title: the gap function is strictly increasing up to the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$. Then $\gamma_e$ is strictly increasing
  on $[0, C_e]$ and continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Continuity is that of $\arcsin$ (a continuous function on all of
    $\mathbb{R}$ in the clamped convention) composed with linear maps.

    For strict monotonicity take $0 \le s < t \le C_e$ and let
    $\kappa \in \{\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1}\}$. Then
    $\kappa s/2 < \kappa t/2$ (as $\kappa > 0$),
    $-1 \le 0 \le \kappa s/2$, and $\kappa t/2 \le \kappa\,C_e/2 \le 1$ by
    \cref{lem:edge_cap_pos}. Strict monotonicity of $\arcsin$ on $[-1,1]$
    therefore gives $\arcsin(\kappa s/2) < \arcsin(\kappa t/2)$ for each of the
    two curvatures, and $\gamma_e(s) < \gamma_e(t)$ follows by adding.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    StrictMonoOn (gapAngleAt κ e) (Set.Icc 0 (edgeCap κ e)) := by
  obtain ⟨-, hcl1, hcl2, -⟩ := edgeCap_pos h h'
  intro s hs t ht hst
  exact add_lt_add (arcsin_summand_lt h hcl1 hs.1 hst ht.2)
    (arcsin_summand_lt h' hcl2 hs.1 hst ht.2)

blocks.label: lem:gap_wall_value_zero
blocks.title: the gap function vanishes at zero length

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_zero
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_zero (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) : gapAngleAt κ e 0 = 0 := by
  simp [gapAngleAt]

blocks.label: lem:gap_wall_value_cap
blocks.title: the gap function reaches the wall at the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$. Then $\gamma_e(C_e) = U_e$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Write $M = \max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ and
    $m = \min(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$, so that $M > 0$ and $C_e = 2/M$; then
    $\kappa_e\,C_e/2 = \kappa_e/M$ and $\kappa_{e+1}\,C_e/2 = \kappa_{e+1}/M$.
    In the case $\kappa_e \le \kappa_{e+1}$ we have $M = \kappa_{e+1}$,
    $m = \kappa_e$, and the two arguments are $m/M$ and $1$; in the case
    $\kappa_{e+1} \le \kappa_e$ they are $1$ and $m/M$. Either way, since
    addition is commutative,
    $\gamma_e(C_e) = \arcsin 1 + \arcsin(m/M) = \pi/2 + \arcsin(m/M) = U_e$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapAngleAt_edgeCap
lean.code:
lemma gapAngleAt_edgeCap {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) : gapAngleAt κ e (edgeCap κ e) = edgeWall κ e := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [gapAngleAt, edgeCap, edgeWall, max_eq_right hle, min_eq_left hle]
    have h1 : κ e * (2 / κ (e + 1) / 2) = κ e / κ (e + 1) := by
      field_simp
    have h2 : κ (e + 1) * (2 / κ (e + 1) / 2) = 1 := by
      field_simp
    rw [h1, h2, Real.arcsin_one]
    ring
  · rw [gapAngleAt, edgeCap, edgeWall, max_eq_left hle, min_eq_right hle]
    have h1 : κ e * (2 / κ e / 2) = 1 := by
      field_simp
    have h2 : κ (e + 1) * (2 / κ e / 2) = κ (e + 1) / κ e := by
      field_simp
    rw [h1, h2, Real.arcsin_one]

blocks.label: lem:gap_surjective
blocks.title: every admissible gap is attained, uniquely
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and $0 < \beta < U_e$. Then there is a
  unique $t$ with $0 < t < C_e$ and $\gamma_e(t) = \beta$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    \emph{Existence.} $\gamma_e$ is continuous on $[0, C_e]$ and
    $0 \le C_e$ by \cref{lem:edge_cap_pos}, so the intermediate value theorem
    on an open interval gives
    $\bigl(\gamma_e(0),\, \gamma_e(C_e)\bigr) \subseteq \gamma_e\bigl((0,
    C_e)\bigr)$. By \cref{lem:gap_wall_value_zero,lem:gap_wall_value_cap} the left-hand side is
    $(0, U_e)$, which contains $\beta$.

    \emph{Uniqueness.} $\gamma_e$ is strictly increasing on $[0, C_e]$
    (\cref{lem:gap_strict_mono}), hence injective there, and $(0,C_e)
    \subseteq [0,C_e]$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_unique_length_of_gap
lean.code:
lemma exists_unique_length_of_gap {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) {β : ℝ} (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβU : β < edgeWall κ e) :
    ∃! t, t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (edgeCap κ e) ∧ gapAngleAt κ e t = β := by
  have hC : (0 : ℝ) ≤ edgeCap κ e := (edgeCap_pos h h').1.le
  have hsub := intermediate_value_Ioo hC
    ((gapAngleAt_continuous κ e).continuousOn
      (s := Set.Icc 0 (edgeCap κ e)))
  rw [gapAngleAt_zero, gapAngleAt_edgeCap h h'] at hsub
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hval⟩ := hsub ⟨hβ0, hβU⟩
  refine ⟨t, ⟨ht, hval⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro s ⟨hs, hsval⟩
  exact (gapAngleAt_strictMonoOn h h').injOn (Set.Ioo_subset_Icc_self hs)
    (Set.Ioo_subset_Icc_self ht) (hsval.trans hval.symm)

deps.label: lem:gap_wall_value_zero

deps.title: the gap function reaches the wall at the cap
deps.label: lem:gap_wall_value_cap

deps.title: the gap function is strictly increasing up to the cap
deps.label: lem:gap_strict_mono

blocks.label: def:gap_length
blocks.title: the inverse: length of a prescribed gap
blocks.body:
For $\kappa$, an edge $e$ and a real $\beta$, let
  $\mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta$ be the length produced by
  \cref{lem:gap_surjective} when $\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and
  $0 < \beta < U_e$, chosen arbitrarily (junk) otherwise.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapLength
lean.code:
noncomputable def gapLength (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (e : ZMod n) (β : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if h : 0 < κ e ∧ 0 < κ (e + 1) ∧ 0 < β ∧ β < edgeWall κ e then
    (exists_unique_length_of_gap h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2.1 h.2.2.2).exists.choose
  else 0

deps.title: every admissible gap is attained, uniquely
deps.label: lem:gap_surjective

blocks.label: lem:gap_length_spec
blocks.title: the inverse inverts
blocks.body:
If $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and $0 < \beta < U_e$ then
  $\gamma_e\bigl(\mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta\bigr) = \beta$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    This is one of the two defining properties of the element chosen in
    \cref{def:gap_length} from the existence statement of
    \cref{lem:gap_surjective}.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapLength_spec
lean.code:
lemma gapLength_spec {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} {β : ℝ} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβU : β < edgeWall κ e) :
    gapAngleAt κ e (gapLength κ e β) = β := by
  rw [gapLength, dif_pos ⟨h, h', hβ0, hβU⟩]
  exact (exists_unique_length_of_gap h h' hβ0 hβU).exists.choose_spec.2

deps.label: def:gap_length

deps.label: lem:gap_surjective

blocks.label: lem:gap_length_mem
blocks.title: the inverse lands strictly inside the cap

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.gapLength_mem_Ioo
lean.code:
lemma gapLength_mem_Ioo {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} {β : ℝ} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβU : β < edgeWall κ e) :
    0 < gapLength κ e β ∧ gapLength κ e β < edgeCap κ e := by
  rw [gapLength, dif_pos ⟨h, h', hβ0, hβU⟩]
  exact ⟨(exists_unique_length_of_gap h h' hβ0 hβU).exists.choose_spec.1.1,
    (exists_unique_length_of_gap h h' hβ0 hβU).exists.choose_spec.1.2⟩

/-! ## Radius form of the cap and the wall

The external four-gap notes work with the osculating radii `r_i = 1/κ_i`;
inversion is order-reversing on `(0, ∞)`, so it swaps `min` and `max` and
leaves the wall ratio unchanged. -/

deps.label: def:gap_length

deps.label: lem:gap_surjective

blocks.label: lem:gap_radius_cap
blocks.title: radius form of the cap
blocks.body:
Assume $\kappa_e, \kappa_{e+1} > 0$ and set $r_i = 1/\kappa_i$. Then
  $C_e = 2\,\min(r_e,\, r_{e+1})$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Inversion $x \mapsto 1/x$ is order-reversing on $(0,\infty)$, so
    $\min(r_e, r_{e+1}) = 1/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$; the claim is then
    $C_e = 2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ restated.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeCap_eq_radius
lean.code:
lemma edgeCap_eq_radius {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    edgeCap κ e = 2 * min (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1)) := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [edgeCap, max_eq_right hle,
      min_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle)]
    ring
  · rw [edgeCap, max_eq_left hle,
      min_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle)]
    ring

blocks.label: lem:gap_radius_wall
blocks.title: radius form of the wall

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.edgeWall_eq_radius
lean.code:
lemma edgeWall_eq_radius {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {e : ZMod n} (h : 0 < κ e)
    (h' : 0 < κ (e + 1)) :
    edgeWall κ e = Real.pi / 2 +
      Real.arcsin (min (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1)) /
        max (1 / κ e) (1 / κ (e + 1))) := by
  rcases le_total (κ e) (κ (e + 1)) with hle | hle
  · rw [edgeWall, max_eq_right hle, min_eq_left hle,
      min_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle),
      max_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h hle)]
    have harg : (1 : ℝ) / κ (e + 1) / (1 / κ e) = κ e / κ (e + 1) := by
      field_simp [h.ne', h'.ne']
    rw [harg]
  · rw [edgeWall, max_eq_left hle, min_eq_right hle,
      min_eq_left (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle),
      max_eq_right (one_div_le_one_div_of_le h' hle)]
    have harg : (1 : ℝ) / κ e / (1 / κ (e + 1)) = κ (e + 1) / κ e := by
      field_simp [h.ne', h'.ne']
    rw [harg]

blocks.title: Repackaging a gap vector as a realization

blocks.label: thm:realizes_of_gap_data
blocks.title: realizability from edge-coordinate data
blocks.body:
Let $n \ge 3$, let $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let $\ell$ satisfy
  \[
    \forall e,\; 0 < \ell_e < C_e,
    \qquad E(\kappa,\ell) = 0,
    \qquad \sum_{e} \beta_e = 2\pi .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    The first hypothesis is $\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$ by
    \cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge}; the third is $T(\kappa,\ell) = 2\pi$ by
    \cref{lem:gap_sum}. With the closure hypothesis and positivity of $\kappa$
    in hand, \cref{thm:convex_simple} supplies
    $\mathrm{IsSimplePolygon}\,(P(\kappa,\ell))$. The four conjuncts of
    \cref{def:discrete_realizes} are then exactly what we have, witnessed by
    $\ell$.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_gapData
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_gapData [NeZero n] {κ ℓ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hℓ : ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < ℓ e ∧ ℓ e < edgeCap κ e)
    (hE : closureGap κ ℓ = 0)
    (hsum : ∑ e : ZMod n, gapAngle κ ℓ e = 2 * Real.pi) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hMA : ModerateArc 0 κ ℓ := (moderateArc_zero_iff_edge hκ).2 hℓ
  have hT : turningSum κ ℓ = 2 * Real.pi := by
    rw [← sum_gapAngle]
    exact hsum
  exact ⟨ℓ, hMA, hE, hT, isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn hMA hκ hE hT⟩

blocks.label: thm:realizes_of_gap_vector
blocks.title: realizability from a gap vector
blocks.body:
Let $n \ge 3$ and $\kappa_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let
  $\beta \colon \mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
  \[
    \forall k,\; 0 < \beta_k < U_k,
    \qquad \sum_k \beta_k = 2\pi,
    \qquad E\bigl(\kappa,\ \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,\cdot\,\beta_\cdot\bigr)
             = 0 .
  \]
  Then $\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa$, realized by the edge lengths
  $\ell_e = \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta_e$, and those lengths are
  strictly positive.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Put $\ell_e = \mathrm{gapLength}\,\kappa\,e\,\beta_e$. By
    \cref{lem:gap_length_spec,lem:gap_length_mem} each $\ell_e$ lies in $(0, C_e)$ --- in
    particular every edge length is strictly positive --- and
    $\gamma_e(\ell_e) = \beta_e$, i.e.\ the gaps of the configuration
    $(\kappa,\ell)$ are the prescribed $\beta$. So
    $\sum_e \beta_e = 2\pi$ is the third hypothesis of
    \cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_data} and the assumed vanishing of the closure
    gap is its second. Apply \cref{thm:realizes_of_gap_data}.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_gapVector
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_gapVector [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) {β : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hβ : ∀ k : ZMod n, 0 < β k ∧ β k < edgeWall κ k)
    (hsum : ∑ k : ZMod n, β k = 2 * Real.pi)
    (hE : closureGap κ (fun e => gapLength κ e (β e)) = 0) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hmem : ∀ e : ZMod n, 0 < gapLength κ e (β e) ∧
      gapLength κ e (β e) < edgeCap κ e := fun e =>
    gapLength_mem_Ioo (hκ e) (hκ (e + 1)) (hβ e).1 (hβ e).2
  refine realizesR2_of_gapData hn hκ hmem hE ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ =>
    show gapAngle κ (fun e' => gapLength κ e' (β e')) e = β e from
      gapLength_spec (hκ e) (hκ (e + 1)) (hβ e).1 (hβ e).2]
  exact hsum

/-! ## The global step of the zigzag argument

Purely order-theoretic — no curvature, no closure, no geometry. The local
consequence feeding `exists_of_high_neighbour` is an explicit hypothesis,
precisely so that this file takes on none of the risk of the unaudited
external local certificates. -/

blocks.title: The global step of the zigzag argument

blocks.tex:
The zigzag argument of the external pipeline is organized as: a family of
\emph{local} certificates, one per consecutive pair of curvature peaks, each of
which either finishes the proof outright or forces a comparison on the
intervening radius; plus a \emph{global} step which observes that those forced
comparisons cannot all hold. Only the global step is proved here. It is
purely order-theoretic --- no curvature, no closure, no geometry --- and it is
stated with the local consequence as a hypothesis, precisely so that the
chapter takes on none of the risk of the unaudited local certificates.

blocks.label: lem:high_neighbour_cyclic
blocks.title: a cyclic family cannot beat both neighbours everywhere
blocks.body:
Let $m \ge 1$ and $H \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathbb{R}$. Then there is an
  index $i$ with
  \[
    H_{i+1} \le H_i \qquad\text{and}\qquad H_{i+1} \le H_{i+2}.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    
    $\mathbb{Z}/m$ is a nonempty finite type, so $H$ attains its minimum at
    some $j$. Take $i = j - 1$, so that $i + 1 = j$ and $i + 2 = j + 1$. Then
    $H_{i+1} = H_j \le H_{i}$ and $H_{i+1} = H_j \le H_{j+1} = H_{i+2}$, both
    by minimality.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_le_both_neighbours
lean.code:
lemma exists_le_both_neighbours {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (H : ZMod m → ℝ) :
    ∃ i : ZMod m, H (i + 1) ≤ H i ∧ H (i + 1) ≤ H (i + 2) := by
  obtain ⟨j, -, hj⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_min_image Finset.univ H Finset.univ_nonempty
  have h1 : j - 1 + 1 = j := sub_add_cancel j 1
  have h2 : j - 1 + 2 = j + 1 := by ring
  exact ⟨j - 1, by rw [h1]; exact hj _ (Finset.mem_univ _),
    by rw [h1, h2]; exact hj _ (Finset.mem_univ _)⟩

blocks.label: lem:high_neighbour_global
blocks.title: global step: some carrier has opposite endpoint defects
blocks.body:
Let $m \ge 1$, let $H \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathbb{R}$, and let
  $P \colon \mathbb{Z}/m \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be any predicate. Assume the
  \emph{high-neighbour consequence}
  \[
    \forall i,\quad \neg P\,i \;\Longrightarrow\;
      \bigl(H_{i+1} > H_i \ \text{ or }\ H_{i+1} > H_{i+2}\bigr).
  \]
  Then $P\,i$ holds for some $i$.
  \begin{proof}
    
    Suppose not, so $\neg P\,i$ for every $i$ and hence
    $H_{i+1} > H_i$ or $H_{i+1} > H_{i+2}$ for every $i$. Apply
    \cref{lem:high_neighbour_cyclic} to get an index $i$ with
    $H_{i+1} \le H_i$ and $H_{i+1} \le H_{i+2}$; both disjuncts at that $i$
    are contradicted.
  \end{proof}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_of_high_neighbour
lean.code:
lemma exists_of_high_neighbour {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {H : ZMod m → ℝ}
    {P : ZMod m → Prop}
    (hloc : ∀ i : ZMod m, ¬P i → H i < H (i + 1) ∨ H (i + 2) < H (i + 1)) :
    ∃ i, P i := by
  by_contra hall
  rw [not_exists] at hall
  obtain ⟨i, h1, h2⟩ := exists_le_both_neighbours H
  rcases hloc i (hall i) with hlt | hlt
  · exact absurd h1 (not_le.2 hlt)
  · exact absurd h2 (not_le.2 hlt)
